Author: Shamim Ahmed

sentences.text:
Counsel for Applicant :- Chhote Lal Yadav,Jitendra Kumar
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Shamim Ahmed,J.
1.
Case is taken up in the revised call.
2. Rejoinder affidavit filed today in the Court by learned Counsel for the applicant is taken on record.

3. Heard Sri Chhote Lal Yadav, learned counsel for the applicant, Sri K.K. Chaudhary, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the entire record.

sentences.text: The applicant, namely-Ashish Kumar Yadav is seeking bail in Case Crime No.12/2024 under Sections 323, 366, 342, 376, 506 I.P.C., Police Station-Kotwali Bikapur, District-Faizabad/Ayodhya.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the present case due to enmity and village rivalry.
No such incident, as alleged by the prosecution, took place.

He further submits that initially the F.I.R. was lodged only under Section 366 and 506 I.P.C.
but there is no allegation in the F.I.R. that the applicant has committed rape with the prosecutrix and later on Section 376, 342 and 323 I.P.C. were added only with the intention to give gravity to the alleged offence.
He further submits that the prosecutrix and the applicant were major and were studying in same college in Ayodhya and were in love affair with each other.

On the date of incident,
the prosecutrix went with the applicant on her own sweet will and they also visited several places like Ambala in State of Punjab.

He further submits that the alleged incident occurred on 02.01.2024 but the FIR was lodged after a delay of more than 13 days' without any plausible explanation and in the FIR the informant stated that his daughter has been enticed away by the applicant no such allegation of rape was leveled against the applicant.

When the prosecutrix was recovered by the police her statement under Section 161 Cr.P.C. was recorded wherein she has stated that the applicant enticed her away from the market but in her statement recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C.
she has developed her case and stated that the applicant was drunk and was carrying a country made pistol.
She further stated that the applicant was accompanied by his friend, they both enticed her away on a motorcycle.

She further stated that she somehow escaped from the shackles of the applicant and landed on Ambala Station, where she stayed for three-four days' and later returned to her home, thus, both the statements are contradictory in nature.
6.

Learned Counsel for the applicant further submits that the allegations leveled in the statement of the prosecutrix recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. are false and fabricated and were given only on the pressure created by the police and her family members.

He further submits that as per the High School Certificate of the prosecutrix the age of the prosecutrix is around 20 years and the age of the applicant was about 22 years, thus, they both were major at the time of alleged incident and were consenting parties.

He further submits that the allegation leveled against the applicant got demolished after perusal of the medical report in which the Doctor has opined that he cannot give any definite opinion with regard to sexual assault.

It was further opined by the Doctor that there were no external and internal injuries on the private part of the prosecutrix, thus, he submits that it is a false case and has been lodged only with the intention to defame the image of the applicant and his family members in the society.

He further submits that the applicant is a bright student and his career is at stake due to this false implication, thus, he submits that the bail application of the applicant may be allowed and he may be enlarged on bail.
7. Several other submissions in order to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against the applicant have also been placed forth before the Court.
The circumstances which, according to the counsel, led to the false implication of the accused have also been touched upon at length.

It has been assured on behalf of the applicant that he is ready to cooperate with the process of law and shall faithfully make himself available before the court whenever required and is also ready to accept all the conditions which the Court may deem fit to impose upon him.

It has also been pointed out that the accused is not having any criminal history and he is in jail since 20.01.2024 and that in the Ashish Kumar Yadav vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko. on 10 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/94890496/

sentences.text: wake of
heavy pendency of cases in the Court
, there is no likelihood of any early conclusion of trial.
8. Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for bail, however, he is unable to dispute the contentions raised by learned counsel for the applicant.

9. After perusing the record in the light of the submissions made at the bar and after taking an overall view of all the facts and circumstances of this case, the nature of evidence, the period of detention already undergone, the unlikelihood of early conclusion of trial and also in the absence of any convincing material to indicate the possibility of tampering with the evidence and considering the fact that there are contradictions in the statement of prosecutrix recorded under Sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. and the version of the F.I.R., wherein there was no allegation of rape against the applicant but the prosecutrix took a somersault in the statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C., wherein, allegation of rape was leveled and after perusal of the medical report, as the doctor in his opinion has opined that no internal or external injury was found on the person of the prosecutrix and her age was found to be 20 years and further considering the larger mandate of the Article 21 of the Constitution of India and the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Dataram Singh vs. State of UP and another, reported in (2018) 3 SCC 22, this Court is of the view that the learned court below has failed to appreciate the material available on record.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The order passed by the court below is liable to be set aside.
10. The prayer for bail is granted.
The application is allowed.

11. Let the applicant, Ashish Kumar Yadav be released on bail in the Case Crime No.12/2024 under Sections 323, 366, 342, 376, 506 I.P.C., Police Station-Kotwali Bikapur, District-Faizabad/Ayodhya with the following conditions:-
(1) The applicant will not make any attempt to tamper with the prosecution evidence in any manner whatsoever.
(2) The applicant will personally appear on each and every date fixed in the court below and his personal presence shall not be exempted unless the court itself deems it fit to do so in the interest of justice.
(3) The applicant shall cooperate in the trial sincerely without seeking any adjournment.
(4) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal activity or commission of any crime after being released on bail.
(5) In case, the applicant misuses the liberty of bail and in order to secure his presence proclamation under Section 82 Cr.P.C. is issued and the applicant fails to appear before the court on the date fixed in such proclamation, then, the trial court shall initiate proceedings against him, in accordance with law, under Section 174-A of the Indian Penal Code.
Ashish Kumar Yadav vs State Of U.P Thru. Prin. Secy. Home Lko.

(6) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the trial court on the dates fixed for (i) opening of the case, (ii) framing of charge and (iii) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the trial court default of this condition is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the trial court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of his bail and proceed against him in accordance with law.
12. It may be observed that in the event of any breach of the aforesaid conditions, the court below shall be at liberty to proceed for the cancellation of applicant's bail.

13. It is clarified that the observations, if any, made in this order are strictly confined to the disposal of the prayer for bail and must not be construed to have any reflection on the ultimate merit of the case.

14. The trial court is also directed to expedite the trial of the aforesaid case by following the provisions of Section 309 Cr.P.C., strictly without granting any unnecessary adjournments to the parties, in case there is no other legal impediment.
